name: Gobir

span.toLabel: the Hausa line at Tibiri, to colonial rule

summary.text: The northernmost Hausa state was Hausaland's shield against the Tuareg. Its kings traced their line through Bana Turmi to the Copts, and they first ruled in Asben, perhaps at Marandet. Tuareg pressure and the rise of Agadez drove them south, to Goran Rami and Birnin Lalle. In the 18th century Gobir became the terror of its neighbours: Soba raided as far as Ilorin, and Babari destroyed Birnin Zamfara and built Alkalawa. It was in Gobir that Usman dan Fodio preached, and Gobir's war on him in 1804 began the jihad. Alkalawa fell in 1808; the Hausa line fought on from Tibiri in today's Niger.

snapshots.title: Gobir in Asben
snapshots.text: The Gobir ruling house traces its migration from Arabia by way of Bilma, where its first king Bana Turmi died, to Asben (Aïr), where it allied with the Hausa of the Adrar against the Tuareg. The kingdom may have centred on the trading town of Marandet. Leo Africanus later describes Gobir's herders, weavers and its shoes “made like those of the ancient Romans”, sold as far as Timbuktu and Gao.

links.label: Cloth and shoes to Timbuktu and Gao

snapshots.title: Driven south by Agadez
snapshots.text: The Tuareg found the Sultanate of Agadez early in the 15th century and replace Gobir in Aïr. The Gobirawa move south, first to Maigali and then to Goran Rami near today's Sabon Birni; some stay behind as the Adarawa. Gobir is held to guard its sister states from the desert raiders.

links.label: Pushed out of Aïr by Agadez

snapshots.title: Soba's wars
snapshots.text: With Zamfara and Agadez, Gobir helps throw off Kebbi's overlordship around 1715. Gobirawa settle in Zamfara's farmlands. Then Sarki Soba besieges Zabarma for three years, crosses the Niger to ravage Gurma and raids south as far as Ilorin, where Gobirawa stay and still have their Sarkin Gobir. He besieges Katsina's Maradi for seven years; Agadez attacks Goran Rami in his absence, and Zamfara saves it by fencing the Agadez army in with thorns at night. Soba's men at last desert him and he dies fighting Agadez.

links.label: Raids to Ilorin; Gobirawa settle there

snapshots.title: Babari: Birnin Zamfara destroyed, Alkalawa built
snapshots.text: Babari murders his father to take the throne and raids Katsina, Kano and Shirra. After fifteen years he turns on his ally Zamfara, though his sister is its queen; Zamfara's captains abandon their king, and Gobir sacks Birnin Zamfara around 1756–1762. Babari builds his new walled capital, Alkalawa, on the Rima, on farmland Zamfara had once given Gobir's settlers. In the same years Katsina's Agwaragi beats Sarki Yakubu and takes his sword.

snapshots.title: Bawa Jan Gwarzo
snapshots.text: Bawa Jan Gwarzo besieges Zamfara's last king in his hill fortress of Kiawa for fifteen years, takes him and hangs his head on a fig tree. Bawa invites the young Fulani scholar Usman dan Fodio to Gobir; dan Fodio settles at Degel, preaches, and teaches Bawa's nephew Yunfa. The Coptic origin of the dynasty may be Bawa's invention, to stop paying tribute to Bornu.

snapshots.title: Yunfa and the jihad
snapshots.text: Nafata (1797–1798) reverses Bawa's tolerance and fears the arms of dan Fodio's community. Yunfa, once dan Fodio's pupil, tries to kill him and drives him from Degel in 1804. Dan Fodio's Fulani and Hausa followers rise; Gobir wins at Tsuntua, but the jihad spreads across Hausaland, and on 3 October 1808 Alkalawa falls and Yunfa is killed.

links.label: Dan Fodio's hijra and the war

snapshots.title: Fighting on from Tibiri
snapshots.text: Sarki Ali dan Yakubu and then Mayaki keep up the fight in the north-east. With the Hausa king of Katsina at Maradi, Mayaki builds a new capital at Tibiri in 1836; the same year Sultan Bello crushes a Gobir rising at Gawakuke. The Gobirawa scatter to Birnin Kadaye, Gawon Bazau and Tibiri, and in 1853 a party under Dan Halima founds Sabon Birnin Dan Halima on the Bunsuru.

today.text: Several Sarkin Gobir reign today: at Sabon Birni, Isa and Gatawa in Sokoto State, in Kebbi, Katsina and Kwara (Ilorin) States, and at Tibiri in Niger.
today.title: Sarkin Gobir

reviewNotes: Marandet, Maigali and Birnin Lalle are not placed; Goran Rami is placed at Sabon Birni.
The Asben ring before 1450 is rough and lies in Niger.
